source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 13 (Form 502SU code u), 15-21; Instruction 13 Line 13 code letter u (PDF page 17); Schedule I (PDF page 22)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 50,550.00 + military retired pay (you) 15,000.00 = 65,550.00. Federal taxable income = 65,550.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 49,800.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 65,550.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 65,550.00. Form 502SU: code u (you, age 58, 55 or older): smaller of military retirement 15,000.00 and 20,000.00 = 15,000.00. Line 13 = 15,000.00. Line 14 two-income subtraction: 0.00 (not a joint return). Line 15 total subtractions = Line 13 15,000.00 = 15,000.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 65,550.00 - 15,000.00 = 50,550.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 3,350.00. Line 18 net income = 50,550.00 - 3,350.00 = 47,200.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 65,550.00 (not over 100,000) gives 3,200.00 each x 1 (Box A) = 3,200.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 47,200.00 - 3,200.00 = 44,000.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule I as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 41,000.00 = 1,947.50; total 2,037.50. (The tax table row 44,000-44,050, PDF page 36, gives 2,039; expected keeps the formula figure.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 2,037.50. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000).
